title: Combination Sum
statement: You get a list of different positive integers and a target. Find every group of those numbers that adds up to the target. A number may be used any number of times. Two groups are the same if they use each number the same number of times.

example.caption: With 2, 3 and 5 and target 5, two groups work: 2 + 3, and 5 alone.

idea.sentence: Pick a number, subtract it from what is left, and recurse. Pass the same index down so a number can repeat, and never look back so a group is not built twice in another order.

jargon.plain: Make a choice, explore everything that follows, then undo the choice and try the next one.
The first candidate position still allowed. Candidates before it are never picked again on this path, which stops [2,3] and [3,2] both appearing.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: a list of different positive numbers, then the target, e.g. [2,3,5], 5

compare.bruteLabel: Try every multiset of candidates up to the target
compare.optimalLabel: Prune the moment a pick overshoots

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Pick any candidate at every step with no start index and no limit check, then filter. Orders repeat and overshoots are explored.

rows.name: Backtracking
rows.note: m is the smallest candidate. A path is at most T/m deep. Pruning overshoots and using a start index keeps each group once.

fast.takeaway: Still exponential in the worst case, since the number of answers can be. Pruning and the start index remove the wasted branches.

stages.title: Start empty
stages.note: path holds the numbers picked so far. left is the target minus their sum.

stages.title: Pick one
stages.note: Push candidates[i] and recurse with the smaller left. Pass i again, so the same number may be picked once more.

stages.title: Skip if too big
stages.note: If candidates[i] is more than left, picking it would overshoot. Skip it.

stages.title: Record
stages.note: When left is exactly 0 the path adds up to the target. Save a copy.

stages.title: Undo
stages.note: Pop the pick after exploring it so the next candidate starts from the same path. Return all results at the end.

edges.title: No answer
edges.why: 2 is more than the 1 left, so nothing is ever picked. An empty result is right, not an error.

edges.title: One number repeated
edges.why: Passing i again lets the same number be picked four times. Passing i + 1 would find nothing.

edges.title: Unsorted candidates
edges.why: The code skips with continue, not break, so the order of the candidates does not matter.

edges.title: Target equals a candidate
edges.why: left hits exactly 0 right after one pick, which is the stopping rule for a hit.

gotchas.text: Save [...path], not path. The array keeps being pushed to and popped, so a stored reference ends up empty.
Save append([]int{}, path...). A plain append(out, path) stores a slice that shares one backing array with path, so every saved group changes as the search goes on.
Recurse with i, not i + 1, to allow reuse. Recurse with start 0 instead, and [2,3] and [3,2] both appear as different groups.
With unsorted candidates use continue when a number is too big. break is only safe when the list is sorted, as in Combination Sum II.
Check left == 0 before the loop. Checking it inside would miss the case where the target is already reached.

recap.key: Pick candidates[i], recurse on (i, left - candidates[i]). Record at left == 0. Skip numbers bigger than left.
recap.complexity: Time exponential: about n^(T/m). Space O(T/m) for the recursion.
moves: Track path, start index and what is left
Skip a number bigger than left
Pick it, recurse with the same i
At left == 0 save a copy, then pop to undo
